title: Design and Extend Shared Helpers
readerIntent: Create a stable helper without hiding dependencies or ownership.
priorKnowledge: Know all current and intended consumers.
summary: A shared helper has explicit inputs, outputs, side effects, errors, performance, security, compatibility, consumers, and override rules.

sections.heading: Implementation sequence
items: Search for an existing helper and owning capability.
Prove several framework consumers and no clearer owner before using nCommon.
Prefer a pure deterministic function; pass required context explicitly.
Avoid network, filesystem, provider, database, secret, or mutable-global behavior in a general utility.
Document compatibility and layer overrides; never monkey-patch globals.
Test invalid input, boundaries, error cause propagation, concurrency where relevant, and all critical consumers.

sections.heading: Security and performance
items: Never add secret-bearing convenience serialization or logging.
Keep high-volume helpers bounded and allocation-aware.
Preserve original safe cause, correlation, module, tenant, and execution layer.
Measure widely used helpers before adding expensive abstraction.
